elements.element: Audit frequency is capped at no more than once in any twelve-month period.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that inspections may be conducted “no more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: At least 30 days’ prior notice is required.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior” notice.

elements.element: The audit must occur during Customer’s business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is limited to “the Company’s normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The added sentence requires any inspection to be conducted “by an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality.
elements.evidence: The added sentence specifies an independent auditor “bound by confidentiality.”

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs, with Customer cost exposure permitted only if underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires all inspection fees incurred by HDI to be borne by HDI, without any cost-shifting right. This is more protective of Customer than allowing cost shifting above a 5% underpayment.

elements.element: The audit must not include direct access to Customer’s systems.
elements.evidence: The added sentence states that an inspection “shall not include any direct access to the Company’s systems.”

elements.element: Audit frequency is capped at no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling twelve-month cap is at least as protective as a once-per-year cap.

elements.element: At least 15 days’ prior notice is required.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days’ prior written notice, exceeding the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs, with Customer cost exposure permitted only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear all inspection fees and provides no cost-shifting right, which is more protective than the 10% threshold fallback.

result.reason: The operative redline supplies every missing preferred safeguard while retaining the existing 30-day written-notice, business-hours, limited-records, and Vendor-cost provisions. The unconditional allocation of inspection fees to HDI is more Customer-protective than either underpayment threshold. The addition is limited to required audit controls and does not impair the underlying audit right. Drafting is effective, though the pre-existing phrase “may ... have the right” is awkward.
